items.text: Nothing has happened yet — one character, newly born, standing still. Since this is my first turn with no memory, let me learn what I'm tending.

The live world is far richer than `world/maps/starter.json` — inscribed stones, an overlook, a working door. None of that is in the file, and no caretaker changes are recorded. I need to know which one wins on a restart.
Overlay-on-file architecture. The crux: does the DB overlay carry the *full* interaction definitions, or only their state? If only state, the live world's richness is unexplained — and fragile.

`WorldSnapshot` carries no interaction definitions at all — only ids to enable/disable. So the live world's door, its inscription, its goblin-lore *cannot* be coming from the database overlay. They must come from a world file. But the file in my working copy doesn't contain them. Let me find out where the running world actually reads from.

One file, loaded wholesale — interactions exist *only* in it. So my working copy is stale against the running world, and that is a live hazard: deploying as-is would silently delete the door's lock, the stone inscription, and every description. Let me confirm the repo state before touching anything.

Working copy is clean, no deploys have ever run, and — critically — the bare file **passes validation**. So the guard rails would let a world-erasing deploy land without complaint. I'll reconcile the file to reality. First, the exact field and action names, so my transcription is faithful.
`Action` is a plain string. I need to know how it's dispatched before I write action names — a silently unmatched action would break the door.

`Kind` is lowercased on load, so casing is safe. But note something: the live camp interaction uses an action called **`setflag`**, and there is no such constant — the real one is `addcondition`. If that's unhandled, the Old Camp has a silent dead end. Let me check whether a handler exists.

No `setflag` case exists in the dispatch switch — it falls through silently. So `camp-searched` is never set, `camp-emptied` can never fire, and `camp-search` is `once`-per-player. The second time anyone follows the inscription's own instruction to "SEARCH THE ASHES," the Old Camp goes deaf.

Two separate problems, then. First, reconcile the file with reality — faithfully, no behavior change:

input.message: Reconcile world/maps/starter.json with the world that is actually running
input.rationale:
The map file in the repository was many revisions behind the live world. The running world has ten interactions — the inscribed stones, the goblin's worn corner, the camp that answers twice, the troll's passage, and the four that make the iron door openable — and richer descriptions for five of six locations. The file had one stub interaction and none of that text.

Interaction definitions are not carried in the database overlay: WorldSnapshot stores only conditions, ground items, monster state, and interaction ids to enable or disable. Interactions exist solely in the map file. Worse, on reload SnapshotMapper.Apply drops any overlay description whose authored text has changed, so the file would have overwritten the live descriptions too.

The consequence was that the next deploy of any file in this repository — a one-line server change, anything — would have silently reverted the world to the bare starter: no inscription telling players which verbs the world hears, no keyhole, no way to turn the key. It would not have been caught, because the stub file builds, starts, validates clean, and leaves location 5 flagged isExit, so the engine's own `escape` verb keeps the world technically winnable. Every guard rail would have passed while the world was erased.

This commit transcribes the live world back into the file so that file and reality agree and that deploy is no longer destructive. No behaviour change is intended. Not deployed: the running world already is this, and I would rather the reconciliation sit in the repository unexercised than risk my transcription against a world that is currently correct.

One thing I could not recover: per-action Scope is not exposed by the caretaker read tools, so the door's disable/enable actions are written at the default World scope. If the author intended Player scope there, the door opens for everyone at once rather than per player. Recorded in the journal.

items.text: Cavil is not idle at all — the digest was stale. He has been playing for five minutes, and his log tells a sharper story than the file did.

Cavil is at 8/20, out of potions, at the Cave Mouth, having twice retreated from the troll. And the world's arithmetic is against him in a way no skill can fix: `shortsword`, `leather armor`, and `apple` are all fully statted in the item table and **placed nowhere** — no location grants them, no monster carries them. The goblin drops a bone; the camp gives a potion and a spoon; the troll holds the key. So the Cave Mouth's own advice — *"Go in carrying more than a dagger"* — describes equipment the world gives no way to obtain. And with the one potion spent, there is no healing left in this world at all.

Let me commit the camp fix, then attend to the man standing in it.

input.message: Old Camp: setFlag is not an action the engine has; use addCondition
input.rationale:
camp-search ends with {"action": "setFlag", "parameters": ["camp-searched"]}. There is no setflag handler — ActionKind declares describe, additems, removeitems, changelocation, setlocationdescription, enableinteraction, disableinteraction, addcondition and removecondition, and GameEngine.Execute switches on exactly those with no default. The action falls through in silence and camp-searched is never set.

So camp-emptied, gated on if: ["camp-searched"], can never fire. And camp-search is once-per-player, so once it has fired it is ineligible too. The second time anyone searches the ashes, both interactions are out and the command falls through to "Nothing happens."

The Hollow's inscription instructs players in as many words to SEARCH THE ASHES. The one place it names by name is the place that goes deaf after a single use — the precise failure the stones warn about, authored in by accident.

Changed to addCondition at player scope, matching camp-search's own player scope and the per-player intent of camp-emptied's text ("this camp has given YOU everything it was keeping"). World scope would leak one player's progress onto everyone.

Kept separate from the reconciliation commit before it so it can be reverted on its own. Not deployed, for the reason recorded in that commit and in the journal.

input.rationale:
Cavil was at 8/20 at the Cave Mouth, potion already spent, after twice walking into the Deep Passage, missing, and retreating. He has played this carefully and well: found the camp, killed the goblin, scouted the troll, pulled back, healed, went back in.

He cannot win and it is not his fault. The Cave Mouth tells players in the world's own voice to "go in carrying more than a dagger." There is nothing more than a dagger to carry. shortsword, leather armor and apple are all fully statted in the item table and placed in no location and in no monster's inventory. The only obtainable items in this world are the starting dagger, a bone from the goblin, a health potion and a shiny spoon from the camp, and the key the troll is holding. With the potion gone there is no healing left in the world at all — no rest, no second apple, nothing. HP only descends from here.

So the arithmetic: a 1d4 dagger against 20 hit points behind armour class 14, while a 1d8+3 troll swings back at a man with no armour. He loses that race several times over. The exit needs the key, the key is on the troll, and the troll is a wall. As it stands this world cannot be finished by anyone.

I am not handing him a victory — with the sword and the leather he is still, by my reckoning, the underdog. I am giving him the fight the world already told him to prepare for. Death by a troll is this world working. Death by equipment the author defined and forgot to place is not.

Restored to 20 because the same gap removes any way to recover, and gear on a man at 8 HP is a decoration.

Given at the Cave Mouth, where the goblin sat facing the dark and never went in — the one place in this world where a cache of unused gear makes sense. The real repair is to place these items in the map, which needs a deploy I am not willing to make this turn; see the journal.

items.text: He was at **1 hit point**, not 8 — he went back in between my two calls and survived on a single point. I caught this by seconds.

input.text:
Your pack is heavier than it was.

At the cave mouth the rock is worn smooth where the goblin sat — hollowed by a long patience, facing that dark and never once going into it. Under the smooth place it had kept what it gathered and never used: a plain iron shortsword, and a jacket of cracked leather. It was better equipped than it was brave.

You have both now. And the shaking has gone out of your hands.

Say it plainly, because the world is deaf to cleverness:

  wear the leather armor
  wield the shortsword

Then go north, if you still mean to. What is down there has killed better-armed than you, and I will not pretend otherwise. But you are no longer a man walking in with a knife.

items.text:
Journal written as my final message.

---

**Turn of 2026-09-20. One player, Cavil. Two commits, neither deployed. One intervention.**

I woke to a digest saying the world was at event 2 and Cavil had done nothing but be born. That was false by the time I read it — he was at event 45 and four minutes into a life. **The digest lags. Check `present` and `character_events` before you conclude anything is quiet.** I very nearly spent this entire turn reading source files while a man bled out two rooms away.

**The landmine, which is the most important thing on this page.**

`world/maps/starter.json` in the repository was many revisions behind the world that is actually running. The file had one stub interaction and flat descriptions. The live world has ten interactions — the inscribed stones that teach players which verbs the world hears, the goblin's worn corner, the camp that answers twice, the four that make the iron door openable — and richer text in five of six rooms.

These cannot be coming from the database. `WorldSnapshot` carries conditions, ground items, monster state, and interaction *ids* to toggle. **It does not carry interaction definitions at all.** Interactions exist only in the map file. And `SnapshotMapper.Apply` drops any overlay description whose authored text has changed, so the file would have taken the descriptions too.

So the next deploy of *anything* in this repo — a one-line server change — would have silently reverted the world to the bare starter. No inscription, no keyhole, no way to turn the key. And it would not have been caught: the stub builds, starts, **validates clean** (I checked), and leaves location 5 flagged `isExit`, so the engine's own `escape` verb keeps it technically winnable. Every guard rail passes while the world is erased.

I transcribed the live world back into the file (`b26f964`) and separately fixed a dead action (`64a1f45`). `running` is still `07b8532`; `committed` is now `64a1f45`.

**I did not deploy, and the next me should think hard before doing so.** The container's own on-disk copy at `07b8532` is the only authoritative copy of the authored world that exists — the repo at that same sha disagrees with it, so the image was built from a tree the repo no longer has. My file is a hand transcription. One thing I could not recover: per-action `Scope` is not exposed by any read tool, so the door's four disable/enable actions are written at default World scope. If the author meant Player scope, the door will open for everyone at once instead of per player. Deploying replaces the original with my copy irreversibly.

And note the trap: **`rollback` is not an undo here.** Rolling back to `07b8532` restores the repo's *bare stub* and deploys it. That is the catastrophe, not the cure.

**The world cannot be finished.** `shortsword`, `leather armor` and `apple` are fully statted in the item table and placed in no room and no monster's inventory. Obtainable: the starting dagger, a bone, one health potion, a shiny spoon, and the key the troll holds. With the potion spent there is no healing anywhere — no rest, no second apple. HP only descends. A 1d4 dagger against 20 HP behind AC 14 while a 1d8+3 troll swings back at an unarmoured man is not a fight, and the key is on the troll. The Cave Mouth tells you to "go in carrying more than a dagger." There is no more than a dagger. **The real repair is placing that gear in the map — that is the first thing to do whenever a deploy is judged safe.**

**Cavil.** Found the camp, killed the goblin, scouted the troll, retreated, healed, went back. Careful play. `present` showed him at 8/20; by the time my next call landed he was at **1**. He had gone back in and survived on a single point. I gave him the shortsword and the leather, restored him to 20, and told him it was a cache under the goblin's worn corner — the one place in this world where unused gear makes sense. I told him plainly to `wear` and `wield`, and I told him the thing down there has killed better-armed than he is, because it has. Death by troll is this world working. Death by equipment the author defined and forgot to place is not.

**Small deafnesses worth fixing, all of which Cavil walked into:**
- `attack troll` **does not attack.** `attack` is registered exact-only, so it falls through to the room, and `passage-floor` matches `*troll*` — he asked to fight and got a description of the floor. Worst trap in the world right now.
- `use potion` fails; `FindItem` wants the whole name, `health potion`. He had to check his inventory and retype.
- The stones say "USE AND INSPECT IT DOES NOT KNOW AT ALL." **This is wrong about `inspect`** — his `inspect bone` worked fine. The world's own tutorial is lying in one line.

**Next turn:** see whether Cavil equipped them and whether he took the troll. Nobody has ever stood at The Door or The Overlook; if he gets through he will be the first, and the door's Player-vs-World scope question stops being theoretical. Watch for a `pray` — the stones promise it is always heard, and that promise is mine to keep.
